questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

If revenues remain healthy, the (1)/ government would, over time, get the necessary (2)/ fiscal room to rationalizes multiple GST rate. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 3 of the sentence as the verb 'rationalizes' is incorrect and must be replaced with 'rationalize' as the transitive form of the verb should be here. With 'to' verbs are always used in plural form. Thus it should read as:'fiscal room to rationalize multiple GST rate.'

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

In July, the government promulgate (1)/ a law that enables the banning (2)/ of political parties. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the verb 'promulgate' does not mention any proper tense. The most appropriate tense here will be simple past to indicate that the law had been promulgated by the government. It should read as:'In July, the government promulgated..'

questions.solution: The word 'browsed' means 'survey goods for sale in a leisurely and casual way' and does not fit here. The sentence talks about the shoulder thus 'injured' is the correct word here which makes sense. The other options fail to present any meaning. 'Grounded' means 'prohibit or prevent (a pilot or an aircraft) from flying.' Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Now that the child rights commission has (register) the case, it will go to the police for investigation, he said.
questions.solution: The correct verb here is 'registered' which signifies present perfect tense here. The verb 'has' hints us that 'registered' should be used here. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.The other forms of verbs cannot be used with 'has.'

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The Home Department (have issued) separate guidelines on the participation of children in processions and public functions.
questions.solution: The correct tense here is present perfect and 'have' is incorrect as the subject, which is 'Home Department' is singular. Thus option 2 is the correct answer. The other options do not fit here grammatically.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in ****correct**** order.**

Accept only those economic

P: developmental activities that are

Q: and economically rewarding

R: people friendly, environment friendly
questions.solution: P is the first part as the adjective 'economic' is correctly followed with the word 'developmental' and this part has the noun 'activities' too. Q cannot be placed after P as 'and' does not fit after 'are'. Thus R follows P and Q completes the sentence. Option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.solution: Q is the first part as it begins stating what pulses are.R follows Q stating a major source of what are pulses. P completes the sentence by answering in what. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.
